'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban insurgency]]
***[[2021 Taliban offensive]]
****[[Taliban]] spokesperson [[Suhail Shaheen]] says that the [[Islamist]] group "does not want to monopolize" [[Afghanistan]], pointing to past failed attempts by countries to do so. Shaheen also says that [[women's rights in Afghanistan|women's rights]] under the Taliban would now be respected, although women would still need to wear a [[headscarf]] or [[hijab]] and have a male relative as a companion in order to leave their house. Shaheen also accused [[President of Afghanistan|President]] [[Ashraf Ghani]] of being a "[[warmonger]]" and said that "no one wants a [[civil war]] in Afghanistan". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/23/taliban-afghanistan-ashraf-ghani-civil-war (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Allied Democratic Forces insurgency]]; [[2021 Democratic Republic of the Congo attacks]]
**Gunmen open fire on a civilian convoy that was returning from a weekly market in [[North Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], killing at least 16 people. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/23/sixteen-civilians-killed-in-eastern-drc-ambush (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2021 Armenia–Azerbaijan border crisis]]
**[[Azerbaijan]] reports that one of [[Azerbaijani Armed Forces|its soldiers]] was killed by an [[Armenians|Armenian]] [[sniper]] in [[Kalbajar District]] near the [[Armenia–Azerbaijan border]]. [https://news.trust.org/item/20210723124345-13j0u/ (Reuters)]
*[[Assassination of Jovenel Moïse]]
**Gunshots are heard at [[Jovenel Moïse]]’s funeral, with [[United States Ambassador to the United Nations|U.S. Ambassador to the UN]] [[Linda Thomas-Greenfield]] cancelling the remainder of her visit to [[Haiti]] as a result of the incident. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/u-s-ambassador-u-n-hastily-leaves-haiti-after-gunshots-n1274852 (NBC News)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Burundi]]an Minister for Mining Ibrahim Uwizeye suspends the operations of several international [[mining in Burundi|mining]] companies, including one running the only [[Rare-earth element|rare-earth]] mine in [[Africa]], saying they were not properly sharing the profits and that the mining contracts signed were "unbalanced". [https://www.africanews.com/2021/07/23/burundi-suspends-rare-earth-mining-in-row-over-riches/ (''Africanews'')] [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/africa/2021-07/24/c_1310081437.htm (Xinhua)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record 38,988 recoveries and 1,566 deaths from [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of recoveries to 2.43 million and the nationwide death toll to 80,598. [https://news.detik.com/berita/d-5654322/data-lengkap-corona-ri-23-juli-kasus-baru-49071-jabar-dki-tertinggi?tag_from=wpm_nhl_3 (detikNews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 15,573 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 980,491. [https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2021/07/23/malaysias-covid-19-cases-soar-back-to-above-15000-cases-six-in-10-infection/1992087 (''Malay Mail'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan]]
****[[Pakistan]] surpasses one million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.brecorder.com/news/40108532 (''Business Recorder'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****[[COVID-19 community quarantines in the Philippines]]
*****The [[Metro Manila|National Capital Region]] and the provinces of [[Ilocos Norte]], [[Ilocos Sur]], [[Davao del Norte]] and [[Davao de Oro]] revert to the stricter "General Community Quarantine with Heightened Restrictions" due to the threat of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant]]. These restrictions will remain in effect until July 31. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/news/07/23/21/metro-manila-ilocos-norte-ilocos-sur-davao-de-oro-davao-del-norte-gcq-with-restrictions-covid-delta-threat-iatf (ABS-CBN News)]
****[[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
*****The [[Philippines]] announces an entry ban for all travelers from [[Malaysia]] and [[Thailand]] due to the threat of the SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant. These restrictions will take effect on July 25. [https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/news/nation/796472/philippines-bans-travelers-from-malaysia-thailand/story/?top_picks&order=2 (GMA News)] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****Thailand reports a record for the third consecutive day of 14,575 new cases of COVID-19, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 467,707. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2153611/record-14-575-new-covid-cases (''Bangkok Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] reports a record 7,307 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 81,678. [https://en.vietnamplus.vn/covid19-7307-new-infections-recorded-on-july-23/205194.vnp (Vietnam Plus)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[New South Wales]] declares a "national emergency" of their state COVID-19 outbreak caused by the Delta variant after 136 new cases are reported in the past 24 hours. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-07-23/nsw-records-136-new-covid-cases/100317006 (ABC Australia)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
****[[Fiji]] isolates 87 crew and passengers on an inter-islands ship due to COVID-19. The ship's people have been the latest of around 4,000 people infected with COVID-19 who have been turned away from hospitals due to a lack of beds. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/447557/crew-passengers-isolate-on-ships-as-covid-19-infections-soar-in-fiji (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cuba]]
****[[Cuba]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 7,784 new cases of COVID-19, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 316,383. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2021-07/24/c_1310081491.htm (Xinhuanet)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
*****The [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]] announces that the [[United States]] has purchased 200 million extra doses of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] developed by [[Pfizer]] and [[BioNTech]], including doses intended for children under the age of 12 years old. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/covid-19-vaccine-doses-biden-administration-200-million/ (CBS)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Missouri]]
*****[[St. Louis]] and [[St. Louis County, Missouri|St. Louis County]] will reimpose their [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|mask mandate]] for residents in indoor public places and on transportation as part of an attempt to reduce the spread of the [[SARS-CoV-2 lineage B.1.617|Lineage B.1.617]] SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant. The order will be in effect on July 26. [https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/564610-st-louis-county-city-reimposes-mask-mandate-as-covid-19-cases-surge (''The Hill'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tennessee]]
*****[[Tennessee]] will resume their [[COVID-19 vaccine]] outreach to minors following a suspension of advocacy earlier this month. [https://www.tennessean.com/story/news/health/2021/07/23/tennessee-restart-vaccine-outreach-paused-amid-gop-pressure/8043482002/ (''The Tennessean'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Germany]]'s [[Robert Koch Institute]] declares the [[Netherlands]] and [[Spain]] as "high-incidence areas", which means that most people arriving from those countries who are unvaccinated will have to go into quarantine beginning on July 27. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/germany-toughens-rules-travel-spain-netherlands-79014732 (ABC)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Montenegro]]
****[[Montenegro]] closes all discos and nightclubs as well as bans all indoor gatherings and music festivals due to an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. Nightclubs could be reopened on August 2, but only for those who have been [[COVID-19 vaccination in Montenegro|vaccinated]], [[COVID-19 testing|tested negative]], or who have recovered from COVID-19. [https://hr.n1info.com/english/news/coronavirus-montenegro-closes-nightclubs-as-covid-cases-spike/ (N1)]
***[[European Union response to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****The [[European Medicines Agency]] approves the usage of the [[Moderna]] [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|COVID-19 vaccine]] for children between the ages of 12 and 17, becoming the first time the vaccine has been authorised for people under the age of 18. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/07/23/european-medicines-agency-the-first-to-approve-moderna-covid-19-vaccine-for-children (Euronews)]

'''International relations'''
*[[China–United States relations]]
**Following U.S. sanctions on [[Hong Kong Liaison Office]] executives, China announces retaliatory sanctions on the [[Hong Kong Democracy Council]] and several Americans, including former [[United States Secretary of Commerce|Secretary of Commerce]] [[Wilbur Ross]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-07-23/china-sanctions-wilbur-ross-others-over-u-s-hong-kong-warning (''Bloomberg'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on long-term care facilities]]
**[[New York COVID-19 nursing home scandal]]
***The [[United States Department of Justice|U.S. Department of Justice]] announces that it will not open a civil rights investigation into government-run nursing homes in [[New York (state)|New York]]. Similar letters were sent to officials in [[Michigan]] and [[Pennsylvania]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/doj-probe-state-run-nursing-homes-york-79026951 (ABC News)]
*[[Madagascar]] officials announce that two French citizens arrested over a plot to kill President [[Andry Rajoelina]] are former members of the French Armed Forces. The Government of France says that it is working with its consulate in Madagascar as the French military says that it has no comments on the arrests. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/french-citizen-among-six-arrested-over-plot-kill-madagascar-president-minister-2021-07-23/ (Reuters)]
*The [[Parliament of Sierra Leone|Parliament]] of [[Sierra Leone]] unanimously votes to repeal the [[Capital punishment|death penalty]]. The country had a moratorium on its use since 1998, after the government executed 24 [[Republic of Sierra Leone Armed Forces|soldiers]] for allegedly plotting a [[coup d'état]] the year prior. [https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2021/jul/24/sierra-leone-abolishes-death-penalty (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Attorney General of Guatemala|Guatemala's Attorney General]] [[María Consuelo Porras]] removed the anti-corruption prosecutor [[Juan Francisco Sandoval]]. Sandoval collaborated in investigations against former President [[Otto Pérez Molina]] and some members of his cabinet. [https://apnews.com/article/guatemala-c6534c39859a1daa6eba2174a8cee80e (AP)]
*A 32-year-old Florida man is sentenced to life in prison plus 90 years for murdering his girlfriend and daughter in 2018. The sentencing judge describes the [[2018 Riverview killings]] as the "worst case [she's] ever seen". [https://www.abcactionnews.com/news/local-news/i-will-be-haunted-by-what-i-saw-judge-in-ronnie-oneal-case-officially-sentences-him-to-life-in-prison (ABC Action News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Samoan constitutional crisis]]
**The [[Court of Appeal of Samoa]] declares [[Naomi Mataʻafa]] as the nation's new [[Prime Minister of Samoa|prime minister]], ending a months-long political crisis. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210723-court-ends-samoa-constitutional-deadlock-declares-new-pm (AFP)]

'''Sports'''
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]], [[2021 NFL season]]
**The [[National Football League]] says that over 80% of its players have been [[vaccination|vaccinated]]. [https://apnews.com/article/sports-nfl-health-coronavirus-pandemic-c642a702bfc1ec00063e74addfe3a9e4 (AP)]
*[[2020 Summer Olympics]]
**[[Emperor of Japan|Emperor]] [[Naruhito]] officially declares the Summer Olympics open. The [[2020 Summer Olympics opening ceremony|inaugural celebration]] was not hosted publicly due to COVID-19 concerns. [https://apnews.com/article/2020-tokyo-olympics-opening-ceremony-8b75b92f36477af48612c70a2b7104e1 (AP)]
*[[Cleveland Indians name and logo controversy]], [[Native American mascot controversy]]
**The [[Cleveland Indians]] announce that the team's name will be changed to the Cleveland Guardians after the conclusion of the [[2021 Major League Baseball season|2021 season]]. [https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/31868331/cleveland-changing-name-indians-guardians (ESPN)]
